blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Wait between attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s), or hand failed deliveries to a delayed queue. When a merchant's endpoint answers 503 or restarts for a few seconds, the five attempts currently run one right after the other, so they hit the struggling server in a burst and all fail during the same short outage. The event is then dropped although waiting a few seconds would have delivered it. Also stop retrying on non-retryable responses (4xx other than 408/429), which can never succeed.
findings.title: Webhook retries fire back to back, with no backoff

findings.recommendation: Use the project's structured `logger` (src/logger.ts, already used by src/events.ts) and log fields: eventId, merchant or URL host, attempt, HTTP status or error. Log a dropped webhook at error level, and add a counter for delivered and dropped webhooks. Today, when a merchant's endpoint answers 500, nothing is logged for that attempt because only thrown errors reach the catch block. The final "dropped" line is a free-text `console.debug` with no status and no merchant, so an operator cannot query it, may not see it at production log levels, and cannot tell a merchant why their webhooks stopped.
findings.title: Failed and dropped deliveries are logged only at debug level, as free text, without the HTTP status

findings.recommendation: Do not await delivery inline: enqueue it, or start it without awaiting and report its failure through the logger. `publish` in src/events.ts awaits each listener in turn, so a merchant that times out makes the publisher wait 5 attempts × 5 s, and any backoff added for R-ops-1 makes that delay longer. Whether this delays settlement depends on how the payment service calls `publish`, which this review could not see.
findings.title: Delivery is awaited inside the payment event listener, so a slow merchant can delay the publisher for up to 25 s
